title: Frontend counts an animal as identified once one identifier is filled in; Design release 1 does not count it until every identifier for that commodity is filled in

finding.frontend: One identifier is enough. A trader who fills the ear tag and leaves the passport blank presses "Save and add another", the animal is added to the summary list as "Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012", and the counter moves on. Only an entirely empty animal is refused, with "Enter at least one identifier for this animal" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:140), which is the rule the obligation states as a requires-any-of over the six identifier fields (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:89-98). fe-animal-identification-saved and fe-animal-identification-at-maximum both show animals saved on an ear tag alone.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 appears to require all of them. An animal counts as entered only when every identifier declared for its commodity carries a value (app/routes.js:1526-1532), so a cattle animal needs both an ear tag and a passport. A partly filled animal is not refused and no error is shown — the page simply re-renders the same animal with the values kept and the counter unmoved, and the saved-animals table lists only complete animals. That is a silent outcome rather than a stated rule, which is what makes this finding uncertain.
finding.difference: This is disputed because the two sources of the requirement disagree, and the two readings imply opposite work: if all identifiers are required, Frontend has to change its requires-any-of to a requires-all per commodity and write the error copy for it; if they are not, Frontend is already right and this finding should be struck. Design release 1's behaviour is not in doubt — its entry form holds a trader on an animal until every identifier for that commodity carries a value, and its saved list only ever shows complete animals. What is in doubt is whether that behaviour states a requirement, because the data-fields specification Frontend implements says the opposite in words: the obligation carries the V4 line "Field Block - Mandatory to Submit - At least one Animal Identifier" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:66-72). The one observation that would settle it is a statement from the design authority on which of the two governs — Design release 1's silent per-field behaviour, or the V4 field block. No capture can settle it; see the correction for why the capture originally proposed here cannot fire.
finding.falsifiedBy: An error message in Design release 1 naming a missing identifier, or a line in the V4 data-fields specification requiring every identifier for a commodity rather than at least one. Design release 1's identifier validator returns an empty error list unconditionally (app/routes.js:1776-1786), so the design has no way to tell a trader that an identifier is missing.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and all four page shots for the two identification screens on each side. Traced Design release 1's save path end to end rather than inferring it: app/routes.js:10352-10401 saves whatever was typed with no validation, app/routes.js:1589-1603 then makes the first incomplete animal the active one again so the counter does not move, and app/routes.js:1622-1626 filters the saved list to complete animals only. Read the frontend obligation at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:61-101 and the error copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:140. Confirmed the quoted summary row in capture/html/frontend/fe-animal-identification-saved.html:134-135. Band stays disputed; the difference slot is rewritten and the falsifier replaced, both recorded below.
finding.correction: The claim about both applications is correct and both descriptions are accurate — the verification traced Design release 1's save, re-render and filter and found exactly what the prototype slot describes. Two things were wrong with how the dispute was framed, and both are fixed. (1) The settling observation could never have fired. It proposed capturing Design release 1 after entering one identifier and looking for a saved row with an empty Passport column, but the saved list is filtered to complete animals unconditionally at app/routes.js:1622-1626, so that capture is guaranteed to produce the "it holds" branch whatever the design intends. The old falsifier had the same flaw and has been replaced. (2) The dispute was framed as uncertainty about Design release 1's behaviour, and it is not; it is a contradiction between Design release 1's behaviour and the V4 data-fields specification that Frontend's obligation cites in a comment at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:66-72, which states at least one identifier per animal. That is a real conflict between two requirement sources and it is what keeps the band at disputed. Worth noting alongside: Design release 1's own submit gate is weaker still, needing only one complete animal per species and only when more than one species is selected (app/routes.js:1514-1523).
